name: Cauliflower Shawarma
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a large baking tray. Cut 100 g red onion into wedges and the remaining 80 g into thin slices. Combine the thin slices with vinegar, sugar and 1 g salt; massage briefly and leave to quick-pickle while the cauliflower roasts.

Dry the cauliflower florets well. Toss them and the onion wedges with 30 ml olive oil, cumin, ground coriander, smoked paprika and 4 g salt. Spread in one layer on the hot tray and roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until tender with deeply browned edges; crowding the tray will steam the vegetables.

Whisk tahini with 30 ml lemon juice, minced garlic, 2 g salt and the water, adding the water gradually until a pourable sauce forms. Mix the diced cucumber and tomato with the remaining 15 ml lemon juice, 10 ml olive oil and half the parsley. Drain the pickled onion slices.

Warm the four pita flatbreads for 2 minutes in the oven or briefly in a dry pan so they bend easily. Divide the roasted cauliflower and onion wedges among the breads. Add the cucumber-tomato salad and a small tangle of drained pink pickled onion to each.

Spoon the tahini sauce over the filling and scatter the remaining parsley. Fold the pitas around the cauliflower and serve immediately while the roasted florets are hot and the salad crisp. The cauliflower should remain visible as the main filling.
tips: Dry cauliflower and use a large hot tray for browned rather than steamed florets. The reviewed photo shows spiced roasted cauliflower as the dominant filling in soft pita with roasted and pickled onion, cucumber, tomato, parsley and pale tahini sauce.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
